Things 1–10: Foundations of Data Engineering

第 1 章（共 10 章）：数据工程的基础观念（第 1–10 篇）

1. A (Book) Case for Eventual Consistency以书店为例谈最终一致性

Denise Koessler Gosnell, PhD

丹妮丝·科斯勒·戈斯内尔 博士

Consider the life of owning a bookstore. At some point, you will want to set up a system that maintains an inventory of all the books in your store.

试想一下经营一家书店的日常。在某个时候，你会想要建立一套系统，来维护店里所有图书的库存。

In the store's early days, you selected a system that was designed for about 1,000 books at one location. This system updates a book's record during a customer's checkout. When a customer approaches the counter to buy a book, your inventory system does the following:

开店初期，你选了一套为单店约 1000 本书设计的系统。它会在顾客结账时更新某本书的记录。当顾客走到柜台前买一本书时，你的库存系统会做以下几件事：

  1. Checks your ledgers for inventory details
    查看账簿，核对库存明细
  2. Records the new purchase
    记录这笔新的购买
  3. Updates all the records
    更新所有相关记录
  4. Returns a receipt to the customer
    向顾客返回收据

The receipt confirms both the customer's purchase and that your inventory system is up-to-date. This type of inventory system requires all of your transactions to have strong consistency. In this sense, strong consistency refers to all accesses to the store's inventory being processed sequentially and read from the same state in your store's inventory system.

这张收据既确认了顾客的购买，也确认了你的库存系统是最新的。这类库存系统要求所有事务都具备强一致性。这里所说的强一致性，是指对门店库存的所有访问都按顺序处理，并且读取的是库存系统中的同一状态。

Well, good news, store owner! The book business is booming, and you are opening multiple stores to address your growing customer base. In this world, how do you maintain your company's inventory across multiple stores?

好消息来了，店主！书业生意兴隆，你要开多家分店来应对不断增长的顾客群。在这种局面下，你要如何在多家分店之间维护公司的库存？

Maybe you consider rearchitecting your current system. You decide to have one master register in your first store. Then, all of your other stores will have a new register that connects to the master.

也许你考虑重构现有系统。你决定在第一家店里设一台主收银机，然后其他所有分店都用一台新收银机连接到这台主机。

1 Denise Gosnell would like to thank David Bechberger for his contributions to this chapter.

注 1：丹妮丝·戈斯内尔感谢 David Bechberger 对本章的贡献。

— p.17 —

This new system works great... until you lose power to your master register. Now all of the customers at all of your stores are blocked from making a single purchase. Your lines are long and stagnant.

这套新系统运转得很好……直到主收银机断电。这一刻，所有分店的所有顾客都无法完成哪怕一笔购买。队伍排得很长，而且停滞不前。

Are you going to let your customers walk away frustrated when your queue takes too long to process? To resolve this, maybe you decide that validating and updating your store's inventory can be done in a different way.

当队伍处理太慢时，你愿意让顾客失望地走开吗？为了解决这个问题，也许你决定换一种方式来校验和更新门店库存。

Maybe this time you consider updating your ledgers on a daily basis. In this new system, at nightly close, you update the inventory of your books by counting all of them in each store and validating that each title you expect is on your shelves. Each night, your stores' shelves pass their tests, and you can go home resting assured that your books are balanced.

这一次，也许你考虑每天更新一次账簿。在这套新系统里，每晚打烊时，你通过清点每家店里所有的书、核对每一本你预期应在架的书是否真的在架，来更新库存。每晚各家门店的书架都通过检查，你就可以安心回家，确信账实相符。

This second type of inventory system plans for all of your transactions to have eventual consistency. Each access to your store's inventory is processed in parallel and logs an update to your book's inventory system. Eventually, all accesses about a particular book will return the last updated value.

第二种库存系统让所有事务都具备最终一致性。对门店库存的每次访问都并行处理，并向图书库存系统记录一条更新日志。最终，对某一本特定图书的所有访问都会返回最近一次更新后的值。

And what happens if a customer goes to look for a title that isn't on your shelves? Well, you can address it then.

那如果顾客来找一本不在架上的书怎么办？嗯，到时候再处理就是了。

Addressing inconsistencies when they are found is like read repair in a distributed system. Only when you find an inconsistency do you kick off the heavier process to update state across all of your ledgers. During this process, you can inspect your sales logs to see whether the records are up-to-date. The result of these multiple inspections of state is to ensure that your records are up-to-date and consistent.

在发现不一致时再去处理，类似于分布式系统中的读修复（read repair）。只有在发现不一致时，你才启动那个更重的流程，去跨所有账簿更新状态。在这个过程中，你可以查看销售日志，核对记录是否为最新。这多次状态检查的结果，就是确保你的记录是最新且一致的。

Is this process good enough for you? For systems that have to trade high-volume processing for state consistency, yes.

这个流程对你来说够好吗？对于那些必须用状态一致性来换取高并发处理能力的系统来说，答案是肯定的。

Swapping to an eventually consistent system with read repair to address inconsistencies will keep your customers from the peril of long lines at the register. And it will keep your architects feeling less stress about protecting the availability of your master register's database.

切换到一套带读修复、在发现不一致时再处理的最终一致性系统，可以让你的顾客免受收银台排长队之苦，也能让架构师们不再为保护主收银机数据库的可用性而倍感压力。

Loosely speaking, the two approaches to keeping inventory in your store represent two schools of thought. They describe two different architectures: one that is strongly consistent (addressing scale with client/server–style architectures) and another that is eventually consistent (handling high-volume transactions and resolving stateful inconsistencies when they are found).

宽泛地说，店里维护库存的这两种方式代表了两种思想流派。它们描述了两种不同的架构：一种是强一致性的（用客户端/服务器风格的架构来应对规模扩展），另一种是最终一致性的（处理高并发事务，并在发现有状态的不一致时再解决）。

So for the system you are designing, what school of thought do you want to plan with?

那么，对于你正在设计的系统，你想用哪一种思想流派来做规划呢？

— p.18 —

2. A/B and How to Be如何做好 A/B 测试

Sonia Mehta

索尼娅·梅塔

At its core, A/B testing is a method of comparing two versions of something, to see which one performs better. A very simple example of this is adjusting the location of an ecommerce site's shopping cart image from the top right to the bottom right. Perhaps some team members believe moving it to the bottom will lead to fewer abandoned carts. Depending on the size and nature of the experiment, data engineering may be involved with everything from the instrumentation and tracking to the analysis.

A/B 测试的核心，是一种比较某事物两个版本、看哪个表现更好的方法。一个非常简单的例子是：把电商网站购物车图标的位置从右上角移到右下角。也许有些团队成员认为把它移到底部会减少放弃购物车的情况。根据实验规模和性质的不同，数据工程可能会参与从埋点、跟踪到分析的全部环节。

Related to this topic, it's important to know that third-party tools exist to help set up backend tracking for experiments. Whether a third-party tool or an in-house solution is used, it's critical to validate the results and feel comfortable about the experiment logging.

与这个话题相关，需要知道有一些第三方工具可以帮助搭建实验的后端跟踪。无论用第三方工具还是自研方案，关键是要对结果做校验，并对实验日志的采集方式感到放心。

In validating experiment metrics, nuances will always need further investigating. The list can be quite long, but areas that can allow you to quickly detect an issue include the following:

在校验实验指标时，总会有一些细微差别需要进一步追查。需要检查的清单可能很长，但能让你快速发现问题的方面包括：

Sample sizes样本量

If the experiment is a 50/50 split, the sample sizes should be very close to one another. If the experiment is another split, validate the sample size against the expected weight.

如果实验是 50/50 分流，两组样本量应当非常接近。如果是其他比例的分流，则应按预期权重核对样本量。

Start and stop dates (with any ramp-up weights)起止日期（以及任何灰度放量权重）

The experiment may have been slowly rolled out in a ladder, from 1%, 5%, 10%, etc., to avoid a potentially large adverse impact. The experiment may have also had a bug (in design, randomization, etc.) or been run during a holiday period, and data from those periods may need to be excluded or evaluated separately.

实验可能是阶梯式缓慢放量的，比如从 1%、5%、10%……以避免可能产生的较大负面影响。实验也可能存在 bug（在设计、随机化等方面），或者是在节假日期间运行的，这些时段的数据可能需要剔除或单独评估。

User in both groups同时出现在两组中的用户

If a user was erroneously fed both the control and the experiment, that user will need to be excluded from the experiment. (If this is a widespread problem, the experiment may have to be redone.)

如果某个用户被错误地同时分到了对照组和实验组，就需要把他从实验中剔除。（如果这是一个普遍问题，可能就得重做整个实验。）

— p.19 —

Context-specific restrictions特定上下文限制

Depending on the experiment, there may also be specific restrictions on users that receive the experiment. For example, an airline may provide the same experience to all users under the same booking ID. This may create moments of imbalance in sample sizes for an experiment, but should self-resolve.

根据实验不同，对接收实验的用户也可能有特定限制。例如，一家航空公司可能会给同一预订 ID 下的所有用户提供相同体验。这可能在某些时刻造成实验样本量不均衡，但通常会自行恢复平衡。

When changes are made to the experimentation backend process, you should consider running an A/A test. This kind of test serves the same experience to all users. Its purpose is to ensure that the instrumentation and logging are collecting correctly. When an experiment is live, discerning whether a tracking error is present can be difficult, because it can get masked by the experiment results themselves. Conversely, the error could be easy to detect, but if it's detected after an experiment has gone live, the experiment will likely need to be paused to correct for the issue and then reinitiated, losing valuable time.

当对实验后端流程做改动时，应考虑跑一次 A/A 测试。这种测试向所有用户提供完全相同的体验，目的是确认埋点和日志采集是否正确。实验上线后，要判断是否存在跟踪错误会比较困难，因为它可能被实验结果本身掩盖。反过来，错误可能很容易被发现，但如果是在实验上线之后才发现，实验很可能就得暂停、修正问题再重新开始，白白损失宝贵时间。

Expect most experiments to fail. Netflix considers 90% of what it tries to be wrong. Knowing this, expect a lot of questions! Expect questions around the accuracy of the instrumentation and logging. When you see a dramatic improvement with an experiment, be skeptical. You may want to reevaluate the results and analyze again on the full rollout.

要预期大多数实验都会失败。Netflix 认为自己尝试的东西里有 90% 是错的。明白这一点，就要预期会有大量问题！预期会有关于埋点和日志准确性的各种疑问。当你看到某个实验带来戏剧性的提升时，要保持怀疑。你可能需要重新评估结果，并在全量发布后再分析一遍。

Lastly, don't be hard on yourself! Experimentation is complex, and as you continue to work in the field, you'll learn more and be able to better triage questions.

最后，别对自己太苛刻！实验本身很复杂，随着你在这个领域继续做下去，你会学到更多，也能更好地对问题分类处理。

1 See Do It Wrong Quickly: How the Web Changes the Old Marketing Rules by Mike Moran (IBM Press).

注 1：参见 Mike Moran 所著《Do It Wrong Quickly: How the Web Changes the Old Marketing Rules》（IBM Press）。

— p.20 —

3. About the Storage Layer谈谈存储层

Julien Le Dem

朱利安·勒·戴姆

The main purpose of abstractions in software is to hide complexity. Just as we prove mathematical theorems by using other theorems that have previously been proven, we build software on top of abstraction layers without needing to know exactly how they are implemented. We may understand them; we just don't need to have every detail in mind when we use them, freeing up our thoughts to concentrate on what we're trying to achieve.

软件中抽象的主要目的，是隐藏复杂性。就像我们用已经证明过的定理去证明新定理一样，我们在抽象层之上构建软件，而不需要确切知道它们内部是怎么实现的。我们或许理解它们，但在使用时不必把每个细节都装在脑子里，从而把思维解放出来，专注于我们想要达成的目标。

That said, it is useful (but not necessary) to actually go through these details at least once. Understanding assembly language or compilers makes us better programmers, even if we don't fiddle with them on a day-to-day basis. The same is true of the storage layer of a database or any data-processing framework.

话虽如此，实际把这些细节过一遍是有益的（虽然不是必需的）。理解汇编语言或编译器会让我们成为更好的程序员，哪怕我们日常并不摆弄它们。数据库或任何数据处理框架的存储层也是同理。

This storage layer is what provides the familiar two-dimensional table abstraction on top of a linear persistence layer. For example, while writing SQL, we focus on defining constraints that define a result (joins, filters, etc.) without needing to know the data format or layout. The optimizer will figure out an efficient way to produce the correct result.

存储层正是在一个线性持久化层之上，提供了我们熟悉的二维表抽象。例如，写 SQL 时，我们专注于定义决定结果的约束（连接、过滤等），而不需要知道数据格式或布局。优化器会自己找出一种高效方式来产出正确结果。

A naive query engine would load the data in memory and then apply filters and other expressions. Naturally, we want to avoid loading anything that will be discarded as part of query processing. This saves I/O cost as well as CPU cost by avoiding the subsequent deserialization. We also want to reduce the data footprint, so the data costs less to store and is faster to retrieve. A combination of encodings and compression provides a trade-off between decreasing I/O cost and increasing CPU cost. The throughput of the storage will dictate how much CPU to use, and cheap decoding techniques are paramount.

一个朴素的查询引擎会把数据全部载入内存，再施加过滤和其他表达式。很自然地，我们希望避免载入那些在查询处理中会被丢弃的数据。这样既省了 I/O 开销，也因为避免了后续的反序列化而省了 CPU 开销。我们还希望减小数据占用，让数据存储成本更低、检索更快。编码与压缩的组合，在降低 I/O 成本和增加 CPU 成本之间提供了一种权衡。存储的吞吐量会决定该使用多少 CPU，而廉价的解码技术至关重要。

Those implementation details are usually hidden behind what is commonly known as pushdowns. These push query operations into the storage layer to minimize the cost of loading the data. They come in a few flavors.

这些实现细节通常隐藏在所谓的“下推”（pushdown）背后。下推把查询操作推到存储层里去执行，以最小化载入数据的代价。下推有几种不同形式。

— p.21 —

First, a projection pushdown consists of reading only the columns requested. Second, a predicate pushdown consists of avoiding deserializing rows that are going to be discarded by a filter. Lastly, partial aggregations and function/expression evaluation can be pushed down to avoid materializing intermediary data. They define our abstraction: What columns do you need? How do you filter the rows? What expression do you apply to them?

第一种，投影下推（projection pushdown）：只读取被请求的列。第二种，谓词下推（predicate pushdown）：避免对那些会被过滤掉的行做反序列化。最后，部分聚合以及函数/表达式求值也可以下推，以避免物化中间数据。它们定义了我们的抽象：你需要哪些列？你如何过滤行？你对行施加什么表达式？

Various storage characteristics will impact the performance of pushdowns. Columnar layouts (for example, in Apache Parquet) enable projection pushdowns and better encodings and compression. Statistics (like minimum and maximum values) at different levels of granularity enable predicate pushdowns. For example, if the max value for a row group is smaller than any value that can match a filter, we can skip reading and deserializing it entirely. Sorting and partitioning data—possibly on different columns (as enabled by Apache Iceberg)—will make both compression and predicate pushdowns more efficient, since statistics will more precisely narrow the data to read.

不同的存储特性会影响下推的性能。列式布局（例如 Apache Parquet 中的）支持投影下推，并带来更好的编码和压缩。不同粒度层级上的统计信息（比如最小值和最大值）支持谓词下推。例如，如果某个行组（row group）的最大值都小于过滤条件所能匹配的任何值，我们就可以完全跳过读取和反序列化它。对数据排序和分区——甚至可以按不同列（如 Apache Iceberg 所支持的那样）——会让压缩和谓词下推都更高效，因为统计信息能更精确地缩小需要读取的数据范围。

— p.22 —

4. Analytics as the Secret Glue for Microservice Architectures分析能力：微服务架构背后的秘密胶水

Elias Nema

伊莱亚斯·内马

Recently, we've seen a major shift toward microservice architectures. Driven by the industry's most successful companies, this allowed teams to have fewer dependencies, move faster, and scale more easily. But, of course, it also introduced challenges. Most are related to the architecture's distributed nature and the increased cost of communication.

最近，我们看到行业出现了向微服务架构的重大转向。在业内最成功公司的推动下，这种架构让团队之间依赖更少、推进更快、扩展更容易。但它当然也带来了挑战。大多数挑战与架构的分布式本质以及通信成本的上升有关。

Lots of progress has been made to overcome these challenges, mostly in the areas of system observability and operations. The journey itself is treated as a technical problem to solve. Analytics is often overlooked as something not having a direct relation to the system design. However, the heterogeneous nature of microservices makes a perfect case for data analysis.

为克服这些挑战，业界已经做了大量工作，主要集中在系统可观测性和运维领域。这一旅程本身被当作一个待解决的技术问题。数据分析则常常被忽视，被认为与系统设计没有直接关系。然而，微服务的异构本质恰恰为数据分析提供了绝佳场景。

That's how data warehouses were born, after all—as central repositories of integrated data from one or more disparate sources. In a distributed setup, the role of the company-wide analytical platform can be immense. Let's look at an example.

数据仓库说到底就是这样诞生的——作为来自一个或多个异构来源的整合数据的中央存储库。在分布式架构中，全公司分析平台的作用可能非常巨大。我们来看一个例子。

Imagine that your team releases a feature. You run an experiment and notice that the feature drives up your team's target key performance indicator (KPI). That's great. Should you roll it out for the entire user base? Sure, roll out, celebrate, and go home. What if, however, at the same time, another KPI for a different team goes down? This might happen when you cannibalize a channel or introduce major behavior changes on a platform. Would you want to release this feature now?

设想你的团队发布了一个功能。你跑了一个实验，发现这个功能拉高了你们团队的目标关键绩效指标（KPI）。太好了。那要不要把它全量推给所有用户？当然，全量发布、庆祝一下、回家。然而，如果与此同时，另一个团队的另一个 KPI 却下降了呢？当你蚕食了某个渠道、或者在平台上引入了重大行为改变时，这种情况就可能发生。这时你还想现在就发布这个功能吗？

Of course, there is no correct answer to this. Nor is there a template of any kind. Making a decision requires careful planning of the experiment, cross-team alignment, and a willingness to make small dips where needed so the whole system moves optimally, not the single component. Having data provides a common ground for these decisions, allows companies to make an educated guess, and provides the ability to estimate the impact.

当然，这个问题没有标准答案，也没有任何模板。做决策需要细致地规划实验、跨团队对齐，并愿意在必要时让指标小幅下探，以便让整个系统（而不是单个组件）最优运转。拥有数据为这些决策提供了共同基础，让公司能够做出有依据的推测，并具备评估影响的能力。

— p.23 —

Without data, teams might fall into a vicious cycle of pulling in different directions, resulting in a lot of movement with no progress.

没有数据，各个团队可能会陷入朝不同方向使劲的恶性循环，结果动作很大却没有进展。

So which metrics should you think of when starting a new project or planning an experiment? Consider the following:

那么，在启动一个新项目或规划实验时，你应该考虑哪些指标？请考虑以下几类：

Company's high-level metrics公司层面的高层指标

These are the hardest to move, and rarely will be shifted by a single experiment or feature. They are more likely to be altered by the compound effect of many iterations.

这些指标最难撬动，很少会被单个实验或单个功能所改变。它们更可能被许多次迭代的叠加效应所改变。

Team's metrics团队指标

You do want to drive up your team metrics, but the important factor here is to look at them in the context of being a part of a system.

你当然想拉高自己团队的指标，但这里关键的一点是：要把它们放在“作为整个系统一部分”的语境下去看。

More-granular experiments or project-related metrics更细粒度的实验或项目相关指标

These usually come to mind when designing a feature. They should be as detailed as possible so you can measure the direct and isolated impact.

这些通常在设计功能时就会想到。它们应该尽可能细致，这样你才能衡量直接的、被隔离出来的影响。

There might be more metrics, depending on the project. Only by looking through various levels of detail will you be able to make data-conscious decisions and have the grounds for communicating them.

根据项目不同，可能还有更多指标。只有穿透不同细节层级去看，你才能做出有数据意识的决策，并具备把这些决策沟通出去的依据。

That's why, when stepping onto the path of microservices, a company-wide analytical and experimentation culture should be among the prerequisites, not an afterthought. A rich analytical platform can become the glue that connects separate elements of a system. It also allows you to orchestrate loosely coupled components to sway in the same direction.

这就是为什么在走上微服务之路时，全公司范围的分析与实验文化应当是先决条件之一，而不是事后才想起来的补丁。一个丰富的分析平台，可以成为把系统中各个分散元素粘起来的胶水。它也让你能够编排那些松耦合的组件，使它们朝着同一个方向使劲。

— p.24 —

5. Automate Your Infrastructure把基础设施自动化

Christiano Anderson

克里斯蒂亚诺·安德森

One of the roles of data engineers is to deploy data pipelines by using a cloud service provider like Amazon Web Services (AWS), Google Cloud Platform (GCP), Microsoft Azure, or others. We can easily use the web console to link components together and provide a full data pipeline.

数据工程师的职责之一，是使用 Amazon Web Services（AWS）、Google Cloud Platform（GCP）、Microsoft Azure 等云服务提供商来部署数据管道。我们可以很方便地通过 Web 控制台把各个组件连起来，搭出一条完整的数据管道。

Considering AWS as an example, we may want to use API Gateway as our representational state transfer (REST) interface to perform data ingestion, a few Lambda functions to validate the ingestion, Kinesis Data Streams to provide a real-time analysis, Kinesis Data Firehose to deliver the data, and Simple Storage Service (S3) as a persistence layer. We may also want to use Athena as a visualization layer.

以 AWS 为例，我们可能会用 API Gateway 作为 REST 接口来做数据接入，用几个 Lambda 函数校验接入数据，用 Kinesis Data Streams 做实时分析，用 Kinesis Data Firehose 投递数据，用 Simple Storage Service（S3）作为持久化层。我们可能还会用 Athena 作为可视化层。

With this example, we have to deal with about six components. Each component may require additional setup. Finally, we have to deal with a lot of identity and access management (IAM) roles to handle permissions and access-control lists (ACLs). OK, we can do everything by clicking the console and linking all the components together; this is the fastest way to create your infrastructure if you just need one simple ingestion pipeline.

在这个例子里，我们要打交道的组件大约有六个。每个组件都可能需要额外配置。最后，我们还得处理一大堆身份与访问管理（IAM）角色，来管理权限和访问控制列表（ACL）。好，我们当然可以点点控制台、把所有组件连起来把一切搞定；如果你只需要一条简单的接入管道，这是搭建基础设施最快的方式。

But if you have to set everything up by hand again, and again, and again, it will require a lot of extra time and provide more opportunities to make mistakes, or even open a security breach. That is why data engineers must learn how to automate their code. Here are some guidelines:

但如果你不得不一次又一次地手工搭起所有东西，就会耗费大量额外时间，也更容易出错，甚至可能打开一个安全缺口。这就是为什么数据工程师必须学会把代码自动化。以下是一些指导原则：

Never use the web console永远不要用 Web 控制台

Choose an infrastructure-as-code tool to do this (for example, Terraform or AWS CloudFormation).

选择一种基础设施即代码（infrastructure-as-code）工具来做这件事（例如 Terraform 或 AWS CloudFormation）。

Make it modular做成模块化

For example, use one module to deploy your API gateway, another module to deploy Kinesis, an additional module to manage IAM roles, and so forth. Most tools allow you to reuse your code in various components (for example, sharing IAM policies to write only once and use everywhere).

例如，用一个模块部署 API 网关，另一个模块部署 Kinesis，再用一个模块管理 IAM 角色，等等。大多数工具都允许你在不同组件间复用代码（例如，IAM 策略只写一次，到处共享使用）。

— p.25 —

Use a version-control system to manage your code用版本控制系统管理你的代码

This is helpful if you work on a team; you can enable a pull-request option to check the code before applying it to the master branch.

如果你在团队中工作，这会很有帮助；你可以启用 pull request 流程，在合入 master 分支之前先审查代码。

Test the code before applying the changes在应用变更之前先测试代码

Terraform, for example, shows you all the changes in your infrastructure before applying them. This allows you to avoid breaking your infrastructure.

例如 Terraform 会在应用变更之前，向你展示基础设施将要发生的所有变化。这让你可以避免把基础设施搞挂。

Use a continuous integration/continuous delivery (CI/CD) pipeline使用持续集成/持续交付（CI/CD）流水线

You can automate everything and make your job much easier by using a CI/CD pipeline.

通过使用 CI/CD 流水线，你可以把一切自动化，让工作轻松很多。

If you have never used this approach before, dedicate some time to studying Terraform or CloudFormation, and then write all your infrastructure as code. The time and effort required will be worthwhile: you will have full control of your infrastructure, and it will enable you to deploy a brand-new data pipeline in minutes, by just executing your infrastructure code.

如果你以前从未用过这种方式，抽些时间学一学 Terraform 或 CloudFormation，然后把所有基础设施都写成代码。所花的时间和精力是值得的：你将完全掌控自己的基础设施，并且只需要执行一下基础设施代码，就能在几分钟内部署出一条全新的数据管道。

— p.26 —

6. Automate Your Pipeline Tests把管道测试自动化

Tom White

汤姆·怀特

By sticking to the following guidelines when building data pipelines, and treating data engineering like software engineering, you can write well-factored, reliable, and robust pipelines.

在构建数据管道时，只要遵循以下指导原则，并像对待软件工程一样对待数据工程，你就能写出结构良好、可靠且健壮的管道。

Build an End-to-End Test of the Whole Pipeline为整条管道构建端到端测试

Don't put any effort into what the pipeline does at this stage. Focus on infrastructure: how to provide known input, do a simple transform, and test that the output is as expected. Use a regular unit-testing framework like JUnit or pytest.

在这个阶段，不要在“管道具体做什么”上花精力。专注于基础设施层面：如何提供已知输入、做一个简单转换、并测试输出是否符合预期。用一个常规的单元测试框架，比如 JUnit 或 pytest。

Use a Small Amount of Representative Data使用少量有代表性的数据

It should be small enough that the test can run in a few minutes at most. Ideally, this data is from your real (production) system (but make sure it is anonymized).

数据量要足够小，使测试最多几分钟就能跑完。理想情况下，这些数据来自你真实的（生产）系统（但一定要做匿名化处理）。

Prefer Textual Data Formats over Binary优先使用文本格式，而非二进制格式

Data files should be diff-able, so you can quickly see what's happening when a test fails. You can check the input and expected outputs into version control and track changes over time. If the pipeline accepts or produces only binary formats, consider adding support for text in the pipeline itself, or do the necessary conversion in the test.

数据文件应当是可 diff 的，这样测试失败时你能快速看出发生了什么。你可以把输入和预期输出都签入版本控制，随时间追踪它们的变化。如果管道只接受或只产出二进制格式，可以考虑在管道本身增加对文本的支持，或者在测试里做必要的格式转换。

Ensure That Tests Can Be Run Locally确保测试可以在本地运行

Running tests locally makes debugging test failures as easy as possible. Use in-process versions of the systems you are using, like Apache Spark's local mode or Apache HBase's minicluster, to provide a self-contained local environment.

在本地运行测试，能让调试测试失败这件事变得尽可能容易。使用你所依赖系统的进程内版本，例如 Apache Spark 的 local 模式或 Apache HBase 的 minicluster，来提供一个自包含的本地环境。

— p.27 —

Minimize use of cloud services in tests. They can provide a uniform environment but may add friction in terms of provisioning time, debuggability, and access (e.g., users have to provide their own credentials for open source projects). Run the tests under CI too, of course.

尽量减少在测试中使用云服务。它们能提供统一环境，但在资源准备时间、可调试性和访问权限方面可能带来麻烦（例如，开源项目的使用者必须自己提供凭据）。当然，也要在 CI 环境下跑这些测试。

Make Tests Deterministic让测试是确定性的

Sometimes the order of output records doesn't matter in your application. For testing, however, you may want an extra step to sort by a field to make the output stable.

在你的应用里，输出记录的顺序有时并不重要。但在测试中，你可能希望多加一步按某个字段排序，让输出保持稳定。

Some algorithms use randomness—for example, a clustering algorithm to choose candidate neighbors. Setting a seed is standard practice, but may not help in a distributed setting where workers perform operations in a nondeterministic order. In this case, consider running that part of the test pipeline with a single worker, or seeding per data partition.

有些算法会用到随机性——例如聚类算法选择候选邻居。设置随机种子是标准做法，但在分布式场景下可能不管用，因为各个 worker 以不确定的顺序执行操作。在这种情况下，可以考虑用单个 worker 跑测试管道的那一部分，或者按数据分区分别设置种子。

Avoid having variable time fields be a part of the output. This should be possible by providing fixed input; otherwise, consider mocking out time, or post-processing the output to strip out time fields. If all else fails, match outputs by a similarity measure rather than strict equality.

避免让可变的时间字段出现在输出里。通过提供固定输入，这通常是可以做到的；否则，可以考虑 mock 掉时间，或者对输出做后处理以剔除时间字段。如果所有办法都不行，就用相似度度量而不是严格相等来比对输出。

Make It Easy to Add More Tests让新增测试变得容易

Parameterize by input file so you can run the same test on multiple inputs. Consider adding a switch that allows the test to record the output for a new edge case input, so you can eyeball it for correctness and add it as expected output.

按输入文件做参数化，这样你就能在多个输入上跑同一个测试。考虑加一个开关，让测试能为新的边界输入记录下输出，这样你可以人工检查它是否正确，并把它加为预期输出。

— p.28 —

7. Be Intentional About the Batching Model in Your Data Pipelines有意识地选择数据管道的批处理模型

Raghotham Murthy

拉戈塔姆·穆尔蒂

If you are ingesting data records in batches and building batch data pipelines, you will need to choose how to create the batches over a period of time. Batches can be based on the data_timestamp or the arrival_timestamp of the record. The data_timestamp is the last updated timestamp included in the record itself. The arrival_timestamp is the timestamp attached to the record depending on when the record was received by the processing system.

如果你在分批接入数据记录、构建批处理数据管道，就需要选择如何在一段时间内划分批次。批次可以基于记录的 data_timestamp，也可以基于 arrival_timestamp。data_timestamp 是记录本身所携带的最后更新时间戳。arrival_timestamp 是处理系统收到记录时附加上去的时间戳。

Data Time Window Batching Model数据时间窗口（DTW）批处理模型

In the data time window (DTW) batching model, a batch is created for a time window when all records with a data_timestamp in that window have been received. Use this batching model when:

在数据时间窗口（DTW）批处理模型中，当某个时间窗口内所有 data_timestamp 落在该窗口里的记录都已收到时，就为这个时间窗口创建一个批次。在以下情形使用这种批处理模型：

  • Data is being pulled from (versus being pushed by) the source.
    数据是从源端拉取的（而不是由源端推送过来的）。
  • The extraction logic can filter out records with a data_timestamp outside the time window.
    抽取逻辑能够过滤掉 data_timestamp 落在时间窗口之外的记录。

For example, use DTW batching when extracting all transactions within a time window from a database. DTW batching makes the analyst's life easier with analytics since there can be a guarantee that all records for a given time window are present in that batch. So, the analyst knows exactly what data they are working with. But DTW batching is not very predictable since out-of-order records could result in delays.

例如，从数据库中抽取某个时间窗口内的所有交易时，就用 DTW 批处理。DTW 批处理让分析师做分析时更省心，因为它能保证给定时间窗口内的所有记录都在那个批次里。这样分析师就确切知道自己正在处理什么数据。但 DTW 批处理的可预测性不太好，因为乱序记录可能导致延迟。

— p.29 —

Arrival Time Window Batching Model到达时间窗口（ATW）批处理模型

In the arrival time window (ATW) batching model, a batch is created at a certain wall-clock time with records that were received in the time window prior to that time. Use this batching model when:

在到达时间窗口（ATW）批处理模型中，在某个挂钟时刻创建一个批次，批次中包含此前一段时间窗口内收到的所有记录。在以下情形使用这种批处理模型：

  • Records in a batch can be received out of order; i.e., they can have data_timestamps that are outside the arrival time window.
    一个批次中的记录可能乱序到达；也就是说，它们的 data_timestamp 可能落在到达时间窗口之外。
  • The volume of records is really high.
    记录量非常大。

ATW batching is more predictable since batches are created based on wall-clock time without having to wait for all records for a given time window. This predictability allows for more robust resource allocation and tolerance for failures.

ATW 批处理更可预测，因为批次是按挂钟时间创建的，不必等待某个时间窗口的所有记录到齐。这种可预测性让资源分配更稳健，也更能容忍故障。

In this case, the analyst will have to query multiple batches to guarantee that all records with data_timestamps in the given time window are included. But in cases where 100% accuracy is not essential, ATW batching is sufficient. For example, when analyzing daily active users of a consumer internet company by querying usage logs, the margin of error caused by out-of-order records may be acceptable.

在这种情况下，分析师必须查询多个批次，才能保证把给定时间窗口内 data_timestamp 的所有记录都包含进来。但在不要求 100% 准确的场景下，ATW 批处理就够用了。例如，当你通过查询使用日志来分析一家消费互联网公司的日活用户时，乱序记录造成的误差幅度可能是可以接受的。

ATW and DTW Batching in the Same Pipeline在同一条管道中同时使用 ATW 和 DTW 批处理

It is not a mutually exclusive decision to use DTW versus ATW batching. For example, consider a set of records that arrive at different times, as shown in the following arrival_time_table. Start with ATW batching for robustness. Records with data_timestamps in the same time window are actually batched into separate batches.

使用 DTW 还是 ATW 批处理，并不是一个二选一的决定。例如，考虑一组在不同时刻到达的记录，如下方的 arrival_time_table 所示。一开始用 ATW 批处理来保证稳健性。那些 data_timestamp 落在同一时间窗口内的记录，实际上被分到了不同的批次里。

Based on how much delay there might be in records—let's say, three hours—a step in the pipeline called close of books can be performed. This step creates a batch of data for the 23rd hour by looking for rows in the next few batches. The subsequent query is run at a wall-clock time with a delay of three hours (2020/07/24 03:00) because we may have received records until then with a data_timestamp in the hour time window of 2020/07/23 23:00.

根据记录可能存在的延迟——比如说三小时——可以在管道中执行一个叫做“结账”（close of books）的步骤。这个步骤通过在接下来几个批次中查找行，为第 23 点这个小时创建一个数据批次。随后的查询在挂钟时间上延迟三小时（2020/07/24 03:00）运行，因为在那之前我们都可能收到 data_timestamp 落在 2020/07/23 23:00 这个小时窗口内的记录。

The closed_books_table for the 23rd hour has all rows for that hour. So, closed_books_table is a DTW batched table. The analyst can query this batch and be guaranteed that their analysis is complete for the 23rd hour.

第 23 点的 closed_books_table 包含了那个小时的所有行。因此 closed_books_table 是一张 DTW 批处理的表。分析师查询这个批次时，可以确信自己对第 23 点的分析是完整的。

— p.30 —

The following diagram illustrates how records with the same data_timestamp window can land in separate ATW batches, and how the close-of-books step later consolidates them into a complete DTW batch.

下图展示了：data_timestamp 落在同一时间窗口内的记录，是如何落到不同的 ATW 批次中，以及“结账”步骤之后又如何把它们合并成一个完整的 DTW 批次。

— p.31 —

This example shows that the trade-offs around completeness and latency requirements can be incorporated into the same data pipeline. Analysts can then make an informed decision on when to perform the analysis, before or after closing books. They can choose to query the arrival_time_table to get answers with lower latency or they can query the closed_books_table to get complete answers.

这个例子说明，围绕“完整性 vs. 延迟要求”的权衡可以被纳入同一条数据管道。分析师可以在了解情况后，决定什么时候做分析——是在结账之前还是之后。他们可以选择查询 arrival_time_table 以获得延迟更低的答案，也可以查询 closed_books_table 以获得完整答案。

— p.32 —

8. Beware of Silver-Bullet Syndrome警惕银弹综合征

Thomas Nield

托马斯·尼尔德

Technology job postings often describe the need for passionate people who work hard and strongly advocate their ideas. After all, Steve Jobs was passionate, so maybe that is a trait of successful people!

技术岗位的招聘启事经常写着要找有激情、努力工作、强烈主张自己想法的人。毕竟，史蒂夫·乔布斯很有激情，所以这或许就是成功人士的特质！

But in the data engineering and analytics world, passionate people often have a strong opinion about using a certain platform. We all have encountered this person: the one who zealously promotes Apache Spark or pushes to have all data wrangling work done in Alteryx Designer. There is a strong emphasis on the tool and not so much on the problem/solution pairing.

但在数据工程和分析领域，有激情的人往往对使用某个特定平台抱有强烈主张。我们都遇到过这样的人：狂热地推销 Apache Spark，或者极力主张所有数据整理工作都在 Alteryx Designer 里完成。他们过分强调工具本身，而不太关注“问题与解决方案”的匹配。

Sometimes this behavior is driven by a desire for standardization and to simplify hiring, which is certainly valid. But more often than not, I have seen people zealously advocate a tool simply because they were passionate about it or, even worse, built their professional identity around it.

有时这种行为是出于标准化和简化招聘的愿望，这当然有道理。但更多时候，我看到人们狂热地拥护某个工具，仅仅是因为他们对它有感情，或者更糟——把自己的职业身份建立在这个工具之上。

To put it simply, it is never a good idea to build your professional identity around a tool. Tools and applications come and go, and what is hot today may be deprecated tomorrow. This alone should give you reason to pause before advocating a technology too quickly. Ask anyone who has done JavaScript.

简单说，把职业身份建立在某个工具上从来都不是好主意。工具和应用来去匆匆，今天火热的东西明天可能就被弃用了。仅凭这一点，你就应该在过快地拥护某种技术之前停下来想一想。去问问任何一个写过 JavaScript 的人就知道了。

Another reason that over-advocating a tool is a bad idea is best described by the expression “When all you have is a hammer, everything starts to look like a nail.” More than once in my career, I have had difficult problems land on my lap that required highly unconventional solutions. While I had thrilled customers, I sometimes had a colleague who wondered why I did not use a preferred/conventional tool to solve it. I had to point out the irony of asking for a conventional solution to an unconventional problem.

过度拥护某个工具之所以是坏主意，另一个原因用这句话来描述最贴切：“当你手里只有一把锤子时，一切看起来都像钉子。”在我的职业生涯中，不止一次遇到棘手问题摆在面前，需要高度非常规的解决方案。我让客户非常满意，但有时会有同事奇怪我为什么不用那个首选/常规的工具来解决。我不得不指出其中的讽刺：用常规方案去解决一个非常规问题，本身就很矛盾。

Hadi Hariri at JetBrains best described this behavior as the silver-bullet syndrome: we expect a single tool to solve all our problems, only to chase the next tool when we are disappointed. Do not fall victim to silver-bullet syndrome and become too passionate about a platform or tool.

JetBrains 的 Hadi Hariri 把这种行为精准地描述为“银弹综合征”（silver-bullet syndrome）：我们指望某一个工具解决所有问题，结果在失望之后又去追下一个工具。不要成为银弹综合征的牺牲品，不要对某个平台或工具过度痴迷。

— p.33 —

Instead, stand back. Be impartial and objective. Realize that different tools may be warranted for different types of problems. Granted, you should strive to standardize tools as much as you can in your workplace, but not at the cost of efficacy.

相反，退后一步。保持中立和客观。要认识到不同类型的问题可能需要不同的工具。诚然，你应该在工作场所尽可能把工具标准化，但不能以牺牲效果为代价。

Do you really want your professional identity to be simply a tool stack? Would you rather your resume say, “I know SQL, MongoDB, and Tableau” or “I am an adaptable professional who can navigate ambiguous environments, overcome departmental barriers, and provide technical insights to maximize data value for an organization”? Build your professional identity on skills, problem-solving, and adaptability—not a fleeting technology.

你真的希望自己的职业身份只是一个工具栈吗？你更愿意简历上写“我懂 SQL、MongoDB 和 Tableau”，还是写“我是一个适应力强的专业人士，能在模糊环境中找到方向、跨越部门壁垒，并提供技术洞见，为组织最大化数据价值”？把你的职业身份建立在技能、解决问题的能力和适应力之上——而不是建立在一种转瞬即逝的技术之上。

— p.34 —

9. Building a Career as a Data Engineer如何规划数据工程师的职业生涯

Vijay Kiran

维杰·基兰

Organizations across every sector are realizing the importance of data and maintaining strong data operations. Its recognition as a powerful business asset has seen the emergence of dedicated data teams comprising full-time roles for data scientists, architects, analysts, and, crucially, data engineers. In this chapter, we'll take a look at how aspiring professionals can take that all-important step onto the data engineer career ladder.

各行各业的组织都在认识到数据以及保持强有力数据运营的重要性。随着数据被视为一种强大的业务资产，专门的数据团队开始出现，团队中包括数据科学家、架构师、分析师等全职岗位，以及至关重要的数据工程师。在本章中，我们将看一看有抱负的专业人士如何迈出那关键的一步，踏上数据工程师的职业阶梯。

Data engineering encompasses many overlapping disciplines. It is hard to chart a single route to becoming a data engineer. Studies in areas like information and communications technology (ICT) or software engineering will help, but I've also seen amazing data engineers with degrees in physics and mathematics. Career paths are also varied. Strong data engineers on my team have joined from roles as diverse as sales, operations, and even marketing. As long as you have basic experience in writing small scripts and running data-cleansing projects, you should be ready to take your first steps into the world of data engineering.

数据工程涵盖许多相互交叉的学科。很难画出一条单一的路线来说明如何成为数据工程师。学习信息与通信技术（ICT）或软件工程等领域会有帮助，但我也见过物理学和数学出身的优秀数据工程师。职业路径同样多样。我团队里优秀的数据工程师，来自销售、运营甚至市场等五花八门的岗位。只要你有编写小脚本、做数据清洗项目的基础经验，就已经准备好迈出进入数据工程世界的第一步了。

So, if background isn't so important, what are some of the skills an aspiring data engineer needs to succeed? Three standout skills will give you an important head start.

那么，如果背景没那么重要，一个有抱负的数据工程师要成功需要具备哪些技能呢？有三项突出的技能会让你领先一大步。

The first of these is solid experience across the software development life cycle. I may be a bit biased here, given my own background as a software engineer, but the skills that working across a software development life cycle gives you are invaluable in the world of data engineering.

第一项是在整个软件开发生命周期上的扎实经验。考虑到我自己就是软件工程师出身，说这话可能有点偏心，但在软件开发生命周期中摸爬滚打所获得的技能，在数据工程世界里是无价的。

Second is knowledge of how to properly use SQL, as well as a good grasp of at least one other static and one dynamic programming language. This might seem basic, but it can't be overstated just how much organizations rely on SQL in their data operations. Combining this with an understanding of how to work with, for example, Python and Rust will give you an important grasp of how great software is built and, ultimately, how it can be applied to the world of data.

第二项是懂得如何正确使用 SQL，并且至少熟练掌握一门静态语言和一门动态语言。这听起来可能很基础，但组织在数据运营中对 SQL 的依赖程度怎么强调都不为过。在此基础上，再理解如何使用例如 Python 和 Rust，会让你对优秀软件是如何构建的——以及最终如何应用到数据世界中——有重要的把握。

— p.35 —

The third foundational skill is dependent on the subrole of data engineering you want to specialize in. For those looking to specialize in data processing, developing your understanding of data storage technologies, as well as continuing to hone your skills with SQL, is key. For those who want to go down a more traditional software engineering route, honing your analytical skills will be crucial, as your main focus will be on big data projects. The bottom line here is that you should decide early on which area you want to focus on and develop your skills to complement that function.

第三项基础技能取决于你想专攻数据工程的哪个子方向。对于想从事数据处理的人来说，深入理解数据存储技术、同时持续磨练 SQL 技能是关键。对于想走更传统软件工程路线的人来说，磨练分析能力至关重要，因为你的主要精力会放在大数据项目上。归根结底，你应该尽早决定想专注哪个领域，并围绕这个方向去发展技能。

My final piece of advice applies to every level, from aspiring data engineers through to established software engineers looking to take the next step up: get into open source! If you're learning how to build and having fun with open source data engineering, you're adding to your repertoire of skills. The best way to get ahead in your data engineering career is to start using open source tools.

我最后一条建议适用于每个层级，从有志于数据工程的新人，到想再上一个台阶的成熟软件工程师：投身开源！如果你正在学习如何构建、并在开源数据工程中找到乐趣，你就在为自己的技能库添砖加瓦。在数据工程职业生涯中领先一步的最佳方式，就是开始使用开源工具。

— p.36 —

10. Business Dashboards for Data Pipelines给数据管道做业务仪表盘

Valliappa (Lak) Lakshmanan

瓦利亚帕·“拉克”·拉克什曼南

Show them the data; they'll tell you when it's wrong.

把数据展示给他们；数据出问题的时候，他们会告诉你。

When you build data pipelines to ingest data, how often are you not quite sure whether you are processing the data correctly? Are the outliers you are clipping really a result of malfunctioning equipment? Is the timestamp really in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC)? Is a certain field populated only if the customer accepts the order?

当你构建数据管道来接入数据时，有多少次你其实并不确定自己处理数据的方式是否正确？你正在裁剪掉的异常值，真的是设备故障造成的吗？时间戳真的是协调世界时（UTC）吗？某个字段是否只有在客户接受订单时才会有值？

If you are diligent, you will ask a stakeholder these questions at the time you are building the pipeline. But what about the questions you didn't know you had to ask? What if the answer changes next month?

如果你足够勤勉，会在搭管道的时候去向业务方问这些问题。但那些你不知道自己该问的问题呢？如果答案下个月变了怎么办？

One of the best ways to get many eyes, especially eyes that belong to domain experts, continually on your data pipeline is to build a visual representation of the data flowing through it. By this, I don't mean the engineering bits—not the amount of data flowing through, the number of errors, or the number of connections. You should build a visual representation of the business data flowing through. The following is an example of such a dashboard.

让许多双眼睛——尤其是领域专家的眼睛——持续盯着你的数据管道，最好的办法之一，就是把流经管道的数据做一个可视化展示。这里说的不是工程层面的那些东西——不是流过的数据量、错误数或连接数。你要做的是把流经管道的业务数据可视化。下面就是一个这样的仪表盘示例。

1 You can find more tips on building data science pipelines in my book Data Science on the Google Cloud Platform (O'Reilly).

注 1：在我的书《Data Science on the Google Cloud Platform》（O'Reilly）中，可以找到更多关于构建数据科学管道的建议。

— p.37 —

Build a dashboard showing aspects of your data that your stakeholders find meaningful. For example, show the number of times a particular piece of equipment malfunctioned in the past and whether it is malfunctioning now. To figure this out, you will use the number of outliers that you were clipping out of your data pipeline. Build the dashboard, share it widely, and wait.

做一个仪表盘，展示你业务方觉得有意义的数据侧面。例如，展示某台特定设备过去发生过多少次故障、现在是否又在故障。要算出这个，你会用到你从数据管道中裁剪掉的异常值数量。把仪表盘做出来，广泛分享，然后等待。

People are drawn to real-time dashboards like cats are to catnip. The day that those outlier values are produced for some reason other than malfunctioning equipment, someone will call you and let you know.

人们被实时仪表盘吸引，就像猫被猫薄荷吸引一样。当那些异常值因为某种“不是设备故障”的原因冒出来的那天，会有人打电话告诉你。

This works only if the dashboard in question is web-based or integrated into the everyday systems that decision makers use. You can use free dashboard tools like Data Studio, or tools like Tableau and Looker that have free tiers. Learn how to use them to spread your semantic burden.

这一套之所以奏效，前提是你说的仪表盘是基于 Web 的，或者已经整合进决策者日常使用的系统中。你可以用 Data Studio 这类免费仪表盘工具，或者 Tableau、Looker 这类提供免费额度的工具。学会用它们，把你的“语义解释负担”分摊出去。

— p.38 —
